medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends lifelong aspirin 75‑100 mg for all IHD patients.
NICE NG185 advises aspirin + P2Y12 inhibitor (e.g., prasugrel) for 12 months post‑ACS.

medications.purpose: Cardioprotective ACE‑I for IHD and hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 lists ACE‑I (e.g., lisinopril) as first‑line for all IHD patients.

medications.purpose: High‑intensity lipid‑lowering to achieve >40 % non‑HDL‑C reduction
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends high‑intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg) for all IHD patients.

medications.purpose: Anti‑anginal therapy; target resting HR 55‑60 bpm
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends beta‑blocker as first‑line anti‑anginal for IHD.

medications.purpose: Blood pressure control; dose reduced due to low BP (98/68 mmHg)
medications.nice_justification: Thiazide diuretic is part of secondary‑prevention BP management per NICE CG126.

medications.purpose: Treat documented B12 deficiency; not related to IHD
medications.nice_justification: Not covered by NICE IHD guideline; continued for identified deficiency.

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive antihypertensive effect may cause symptomatic hypotension, especially with low baseline BP (98/68 mmHg).
interactions_checked.action: Reduce thiazide dose to 12.5 mg OD and monitor BP and symptoms.

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined ACE‑I and beta‑blocker can further lower blood pressure and heart rate.
interactions_checked.action: Titrate metoprolol slowly; monitor HR and BP after dose change.

interactions_checked.interaction: No clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction; monitor liver enzymes.
interactions_checked.action: Check ALT/AST at baseline and after 3 months.

interactions_checked.interaction: Intended dual antiplatelet therapy; increased bleeding risk inherent to DAPT.
interactions_checked.action: Continue for 12 months post‑NSTEMI; reassess bleeding risk before continuation beyond 12 months.

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated with concurrent beta‑blocker (risk of severe bradycardia and AV block) per NICE CG126.
contraindications.alternative: Amlodipine if a calcium‑channel blocker is needed.

contraindications.reason: Increased cardiovascular risk and may blunt ACE‑I effect; patient has IHD.
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol or short‑course NSAID with gastro‑protection if absolutely required.

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m²; if eGFR <30 mL/min, dose of lisinopril and thiazide would need adjustment.
Baseline liver function tests not available – obtain ALT/AST before initiating high‑intensity atorvastatin.
Resting heart rate not recorded – assume >70 bpm; if HR ≤60 bpm, avoid up‑titrating beta‑blocker.
Weight/BMI not recorded (obesity noted) – reinforce weight‑management advice.
Duration since NSTEMI not specified – assume ≤12 months; if >12 months, discontinue prasugrel and continue aspirin alone.
treatment_summary: The plan aligns with NICE CG126/NG185 for secondary prevention after NSTEMI: continue lifelong aspirin, maintain 12‑month prasugrel DAPT, optimise ACE‑I, switch to high‑intensity atorvastatin 80 mg, convert to extended‑release metoprolol 50 mg for better angina control, and reduce hydrochlorothiazide to 12.5 mg due to low blood pressure. Monitor BP, heart rate, renal function, electrolytes, and liver enzymes; reassess after 2‑4 weeks and at 3‑month lipid review. Lifestyle measures (diet, exercise, weight loss, smoking cessation) are reinforced.
